The description of a facial rash sparing the perioral area is classic for Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease), but I need to confirm if she has developed the characteristic "slapped cheek" appearance followed by a lacy, reticular rash on her arms and legs. Has the rash spread from her face to the rest of her body in that specific pattern? Also, has anyone in her household recently had a similar rash or been diagnosed with Parvovirus B19?

REQUEST TEST: Parvovirus B19 Serology.
REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide images of the patient's face and trunk rash if available.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) caused by Parvovirus B19. The clinical presentation of a facial rash sparing the perioral area, followed by a lacy, reticular rash on the extremities, along with the recent prodrome of fever and rhinorrhea, is classic for this condition. The normal CBC results further support a viral etiology without significant bacterial involvement.
